x: Dick Northover was first away, followed 45 seconds later by Don Heath, and then came the others with varying allowances, until Don Brown left the post of honour.
Len Fletcher, an ex Inter-Counties champion, now making a welcome come-back, walked well to gain third place, and others in our team were, Scamell, Snr., Percy Wright and Don Heath.
Young McMullen, walking comfortably throughout, finished nearly a minute in front of Bert East, with Joe Wilson third. The handicap was won by Don Heath with Sid Spencer second and Joe Wilson third.

Jack Rutland suffered with leg trouble during the later stages of the race and dropped back into 3rd position. Don Heath, walking slightly above his usual form, scored another handicap win, with Capt.

Bert Webb and George Bentley, who had walked together almost throughout, maintained their positions at 4th and 5th and after Bill True and Don Heath had been told of the loss of East, they both got down to it and succeeded in carrying our team into 2nd position.

Tasker, rapidly improving, won the Handicap, with Brian Shepherd second and Don Heath third. In the first Open of the Season, Highgate Harriers 7, at Parliament Hill Fields, we entered three teams, but neither Harry Churcher or Joe Coleman were amongst the competitors and with Jack Rutland nowhere n…

These included Charlie Churcher, who developed leg trouble, Pat Sapcote, Fred Herring, Jack Wakeley and Don Heath, so that by the end of the race we had just a bare four left, who finished in fourth position, 2 points behind Woodford.
Back in the field, Don Heath, who had been walking quite well, had to retire at 27 miles. Jack Baker and Pat Sapcote also had leg trouble and they too retired.
Then there followed all in quick succession the remaining five of the “ A ” Team, Don Heath, Hugh McGreechan, “Sir” Harry Shields, Joe Wilson and Dick Frazer.
In the early stages, Jack Bidgood Bert Clayton, Jack Baker, Jack Wakeley and George Oliver, walked in a group with Don Heath and Joe Wilson not far away.
This year saw DON HEATH - a member of our walking teams in the thirties, forties and fifties. For many years he has been living in Cornwall and is now back nearer to London.
